metadata.title: NextEra Energy ($NEE) as a national utility actor: the AI-datacenter power buildout, the FPL/regulated rate engine, and the ratepayer cost-shifting question
metadata.frame: NextEra is the largest US electric-generation owner (~80 GW; the next five largest owners hold 37-56 GW each) and, via Florida Power & Light (FPL), one of the largest regulated utilities. It has positioned itself as the utility sector's biggest bet on AI-datacenter electricity demand - 15-30 GW of new generation for data centers by 2035, a ~$67B pending acquisition of Dominion Energy (the Virginia utility at the center of the datacenter boom), hyperscaler PPAs (Google/Duane Arnold nuclear restart; Meta 2.5 GW solar+storage), and a >20 GW gas pipeline. This block maps NextEra as the POWER-side hub of the datacenter thread (the counterpart to American Water Works on the water side), and grades the central public-interest question: who pays for the grid the AI boom requires - the datacenters (large-load tariffs) or ordinary ratepayers (base-rate cases, wholesale allocations, higher gas prices).
metadata.grade: Capacity figures, PPAs, the Dominion deal, the Duane Arnold restart, FPL's approved rate settlement, and the large-load-tariff trend = FACT (company filings, Reuters/CNBC/Utility Dive/PSC dockets, DELTa/SEPA/EEI tariff trackers). The 'cost-shifting onto ratepayers' claim is PARTIALLY supported and GRADED: large-load tariffs increasingly push direct costs onto datacenters (24 states by mid-2026), but documented residual channels (PJM $13B Q1-2026 regional allocation; system-wide gas-price effects; stranded-asset risk) still reach ordinary bills. 'It's about profits not reliability' = a contested advocacy INTERPRETATION.
metadata.honest_limits: Regulated returns are set by state PSCs, not unilaterally by the utility (FPL's ask was cut ~$2.9B; ROE 10.95%). Data-center load can also spread fixed costs over more sales and, under well-designed take-or-pay tariffs, be net-beneficial to other ratepayers. Whether NextEra's buildout is 'gouging' vs 'the cost of meeting real demand' is genuinely contested and depends on tariff design and whether the AI demand materializes. Institutional ACTION (rate filings, PPAs) is documented; no unitary corporate INTENT is asserted.
metadata.method: Company/IR filings + SEC 8-K; Reuters/CNBC/E&E/Utility Dive/PowerMag on the 15-30 GW plan, Dominion deal, Duane Arnold; Florida PSC rate settlement (Nov 2025) via WLRN/CBS/NBC/PRNewswire; large-load-tariff design via SEPA, EEI large-load list, CoBank DELTa database, Columbia Climate Law, Sierra Club 2026, ArentFox Schiff; PJM IMM Q1-2026; FERC Jan-2026 ANOPR.
metadata.opsec_note: National/systemic framing only. NextEra/FPL are treated as a national power-sector actor and the power-side counterpart to American Water Works in the datacenter-infrastructure thread; no single locality is the subject.

edges.notes: FPL (Florida Power & Light) is NextEra's regulated utility - ~6M customer accounts, ~12M people; NextEra also runs NextEra Energy Resources, the largest US wind/solar/storage developer. Combined ~80 GW operational, the largest US generation owner (next five largest hold 37-56 GW each) (fact).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (company/IR filings; Motley Fool 2026-07; Reuters)

edges.notes: Plan to add 15-30 GW of new generation to serve US data centers by 2035 (CEO Ketchum: 'we'll be disappointed if we don't do more'); 30 GW ~= power for ~22M homes. NextEra is the utility sector's biggest AI-power bet (fact of stated plan/PPAs; the 30 GW upper bound is a target, not committed capacity - graded).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (Reuters 2026-03-03; CNBC 2025-12-08; E&E News; Yahoo/Finance)

edges.notes: Google signed a 25-year PPA (Oct 2025) to buy output from NextEra's restarted 615 MW Duane Arnold nuclear plant (IA; shut 2020) to power an Iowa data center; NextEra bought the remaining 30% stake (sole owner, Iowa Utilities Commission-approved) and targets restart no later than Q1 2029 (~$0.16 EPS/yr over first 10 yrs) (fact).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (Utility Dive 804308; PowerMag; SolarQuarter Q2-2026)

edges.notes: First US restart of a fully decommissioned nuclear plant driven by datacenter demand - the template for treating retired nuclear as AI baseload (fact).

NextEra + Google agreed to explore advanced/SMR nuclear; NextEra cites ~6 GW of SMR co-location opportunity at existing nuclear sites, but management flags 'first-of-a-kind' risk and frames SMRs as a next-decade solution (fact of agreement; deployment uncertain - graded).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (PowerMag; Motley Fool Q1-2026 transcript)

edges.notes: Partnership with GE Vernova for natural-gas generation (paired with renewables+storage); NextEra has a >20 GW gas development pipeline and is developer of two Japan-backed gas-fired datacenter hubs in TX and PA. Gas is expected to be the MAJORITY of new datacenter capacity - the 'all of the above' pivot alongside its renewables lead (fact).

Meta contracted ~2.5 GW of NextEra solar+battery storage across ERCOT/SPP/MISO/New Mexico (Dec 2025), long-term PPAs powering Meta datacenters 2026-2028 - hyperscalers shifting from passive REC buyers to primary drivers of new generation (fact).

Pending ~$67B acquisition of Dominion Energy (announced ~May 2026) - Dominion sits at the center of Virginia's 'Data Center Alley' with ~51 GW of contracted datacenter capacity and customers incl. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Equinix, CoreWeave, CyrusOne. Would make NextEra the dominant US datacenter-power supplier; subject to FERC/state approvals (fact of announced deal; close not certain - graded).

NextEra's buildout (renewables+storage backlog ~35 GW by Q2-2026; gas >20 GW; nuclear restart+SMR) is a leading driver of new US grid capacity - concentrating a large share of national generation additions in one investor-owned firm (fact; concentration concern = interpretation).

The buildout depends on scarce high-voltage transformers, switchgear, turbines, and labor/permitting - the same physical bottlenecks that gate the whole datacenter power stack (Q1-2026: labor+permitting called the primary gas-buildout constraint) (fact).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (Motley Fool Q1-2026 transcript; energy-power block)

edges.notes: FPL reports ~21 GW of large-load interest (mostly hyperscale datacenters valuing speed/reliability/price), in active talks on ~12 GW that could energize as soon as 2028; Florida datacenter interconnection interest grew ~2 GW - more than Orlando's utility peak (fact).

FPL's Feb-2025 ask (~$9-10B over 4 yrs, billed as the largest US utility hike ever) was cut ~$2.9B in the Nov-2025 PSC settlement: +$945M base revenue Jan-2026, +$705M Jan-2027, plus solar/storage step-ups 2027-2029; ROE 10.95% (band 9.95-11.95%), 59.6% equity ratio. Opponents (Office of Public Counsel) peg cumulative increases ~$6.9B over 4 yrs and plan a FL Supreme Court appeal; a typical 1,000 kWh bill rises ~$134->~$137 in 2026. 'About profits, not reliability' = advocacy interpretation; PSC called it a 'balanced resolution' (graded).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (WLRN 2025-11-20; CBS/NBC Miami; PRNewswire 302535029; Investing.com PSC filing)

edges.notes: FPL plans ~$40B over four years in 'all of the above' infrastructure: ~5.3 GW solar, ~3.4 GW battery storage, and a gas peaker (pending PSC approval) - regulated capex recovered through base rates (fact).

The core public-interest question: absent a dedicated rate class, the cost of new generation/transmission to serve datacenters spreads across all ratepayers. Documented residual channels even WITH tariffs: PJM's market monitor found ~$13B of datacenter-driven costs allocated across PJM ratepayers in Q1-2026 alone (a federal wholesale layer state tariffs don't touch), and EIA modeling shows new gas demand raising system-wide gas prices (a cost on bills with no datacenter nearby). Stranded-asset risk if the AI bubble deflates (fact of documented channels; total magnitude graded).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (PJM IMM Q1-2026; Columbia Climate Law 2026-06; Sierra Club 2026; gibboneynuclear)

edges.notes: The main regulatory remedy: special rate classes making datacenters pay their own infrastructure via long-term contracts, collateral, minimum-demand ('take-or-pay') charges, and bring-your-own-generation. Adoption surged - ~24 states with >=1 approved by mid-2026; DELTa tracked 20 approved in 2024 and 53 proposed/approved for 2025 (vs 14 in 2018-2024); >300 datacenter bills in 30 states in early 2026. Models: Dominion VA GS-5 (>=25 MW, 85% T&D / 60% generation take-or-pay, eff. Jan-2027), TX SB6, OH AEP, OR Schedule 96 (fact).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (SEPA; EEI large-load list Aug-2026; CoBank DELTa; MultiState; ArentFox Schiff)

edges.notes: FERC governs interstate transmission + wholesale markets (the layer where PJM regional datacenter-cost allocation lives); its Jan-2026 Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeks to standardize large-load interconnection and cost allocation nationally - the federal complement to state large-load tariffs (fact).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (FERC ANOPR Jan-2026; Columbia Climate Law)

edges.notes: NextEra's 15-30 GW plan is a direct bet on the datacenter-demand bandwagon; if AI buildout stalls, the exposure inverts into stranded-asset / over-procurement risk borne partly by ratepayers - linking the power-side buildout to the AI-bubble and datacenter-backlash threads (interpretation/risk-framing, grounded in the stranded-asset literature).
edges.source: #222 NextEra national (Sierra Club 2026 stranded-asset rec; spec-ai-datacenter-foreign-influence)
